title: Signed evaluation square for reconstructed finite-point Hom
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=R/\varpi^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $B=A_s$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf].
Let $C\in D^b_{ctf}(s,A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], $c=\Gamma(s,C)$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], and let $V\in D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ have a specified isomorphism $\alpha:V\xrightarrow{\sim}B$. Use derived internal Hom and signed Hom complexes [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-pur-hom-complex]. Let $e_C:Lc\to C$ and $Q_{C,B}$ be the actual reconstructed Hom comparison of [lem-coef-finite-point-reconstructed-hom-model]. Put $H=R\mathcal Hom_B(C,V)$ and
$$\beta_{C,\alpha}=Q_{C,B}\circ\Gamma R\mathcal Hom_B(C,\alpha):\Gamma H\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_A(c,A),$$
using $\Gamma B=A$ by constant values. Then $H\in D^b_{ctf}(s,A)$. Let $\mu:\Gamma H\otimes_A^Lc\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(H\otimes_B^LC)$ be the inverse of the canonical point-fibre tensor comparison [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]. With the same unit comparison, the equality of pairings in $D(A)$ is
$$\operatorname{ev}_c\circ(\beta_{C,\alpha}\otimes1_c)=\Gamma(\alpha\circ\operatorname{ev}_{C,V})\circ\mu.$$
On a K-flat representative $P$ of $c$ and a K-injective representative of $B$, the input-first evaluation on homogeneous $x\in P^i$ and $h$ of degree $j$ is $(-1)^{ij}h(1\otimes x)$ on both sides; the Hom-first formula is obtained by the Koszul braiding. For fixed $(V,\alpha)$ and every derived morphism $f:C\to C'$, the comparisons satisfy
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\Gamma f,A)\,\beta_{C',\alpha}=\beta_{C,\alpha}\,\Gamma R\mathcal Hom_B(f,V).$$
This includes morphisms represented by inverses of quasi-isomorphisms, and both the pairing equality and this square use the specified tensor and unit maps. Equivalently, $\beta_{C,\alpha}$ is the coefficient tensor-Hom transpose of this specified pairing, with transposition taken in the closed tensor-Hom structure [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model].

proof.text: The unit $B=A_s$, concentrated in degree zero, is constructible and has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$: it is the rank-one constant module and $B\otimes_B^LM=M$. Hence $V\simeq B$ is also in $D^b_{ctf}$. Apply [cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom] on $X=s$, with $d=0$, to $(C,V)$ and $(C,B)$. It puts both $H=R\mathcal Hom_B(C,V)$ and $F=R\mathcal Hom_B(C,B)$ in $D^b_{ctf}$. Thus the tensor comparison used in the statement is defined.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-finite-point-reconstructed-hom-model] for the exact adjunction $L\dashv\Gamma$, its unit $u_c$ and isomorphism $e_C$, and its flat-term K-flat and K-injective models. Apply the finite case of [lem-pod-point-derived-hom-evaluation] to $c$ and $B\to J$. Its comparison is precisely $q_{c,B}$: both use $q(h)(x)=h(1\otimes x)$ and the same derived representative maps. It identifies evaluation for $Lc$ with coefficient evaluation. By [lem-sf-point-ringed-evaluation-model], the inverse sections-tensor comparison is the section tensor map, its unit is $\Gamma B=A$, and its localization is the canonical point pullback comparison. The comparison of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor] is canonical in the finite sense of [def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-finite-models]: on K-flat models it is the chain isomorphism sending a section tensor generator $x\otimes y$ to the tensor of the final-object sections, which is the map $b$ above. Therefore the balancing map in this evaluation identity is the inverse of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor], with $c$ identified with $\Gamma Lc$ by $u_c$, rather than an independently chosen tensor isomorphism.

proof.text:
Write $T=R\mathcal Hom_B(e_C,B):F\to R\mathcal Hom_B(Lc,B)$. The closed adjunction supplied by [lem-sf-ringed-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction], with evaluation as in [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model], gives its counit naturality identity
$$\operatorname{ev}_{Lc,B}(T\otimes1_{Lc})=\operatorname{ev}_{C,B}(1_F\otimes e_C).$$
Precompose the evaluation identity of step 2 by $\Gamma T\otimes1_c$. Naturality of the specified tensor comparison rewrites its right side as
$$\Gamma(\operatorname{ev}_{C,B})\,\mu_{F,C}(1_{\Gamma F}\otimes\Gamma(e_C)u_c).$$
The triangle identity $\Gamma(e_C)u_c=1_c$ of [lem-coef-finite-point-reconstructed-hom-model] removes the last factor. Since $Q_{C,B}=q_{c,B}\Gamma T$, this proves
$$\operatorname{ev}_c(Q_{C,B}\otimes1_c)=\Gamma(\operatorname{ev}_{C,B})\mu_{F,C}.$$
Only naturality and the adjunction triangle are used in this substitution; no new reconstruction or evaluation map is selected.

proof.text: Put $a=R\mathcal Hom_B(C,\alpha):H\to F$. Evaluation naturality in its target, for the closed structure of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction, def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model], says $\operatorname{ev}_{C,B}(a\otimes1_C)=\alpha\operatorname{ev}_{C,V}$. Precompose step 3 by $\Gamma a\otimes1_c$ and use naturality of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]. This gives exactly the stated pairing equality with $\beta_{C,\alpha}=Q_{C,B}\Gamma a$ and $\mu=\mu_{H,C}$. On the representatives of step 2, after applying $a$ and $T$, [lem-pod-point-derived-hom-evaluation] gives the input-first value $(-1)^{ij}h(1\otimes x)$. The braiding in [lem-sf-point-ringed-evaluation-model] is $x\otimes h\mapsto(-1)^{ij}h\otimes x$; hence the Hom-first convention has the corresponding braided value. The same unit map $a\mapsto a\cdot1$ is used throughout.

proof.text:
For $f:C\to C'$ in the stated constructible finite-Tor domain, naturality of $Q$ for all derived morphisms in [lem-coef-finite-point-reconstructed-hom-model] gives
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\Gamma f,A)Q_{C',B}=Q_{C,B}\Gamma R\mathcal Hom_B(f,B).$$
Bifunctoriality of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] gives
$$R\mathcal Hom_B(f,B)R\mathcal Hom_B(C',\alpha)=R\mathcal Hom_B(C,\alpha)R\mathcal Hom_B(f,V).$$
Compose these two equalities to obtain the displayed naturality square for $\beta$. These are equalities of derived functors, so they apply to inverse images of quasi-isomorphisms as well; no assertion that every derived morphism is a chain map is needed.

proof.text: Finally, the coefficient closed tensor-Hom adjunction of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction], specialized to the one-object ringed site with ring $A$, is a bijection on morphism sets. Its inverse sends $b:\Gamma H\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(c,A)$ to $\operatorname{ev}_c(b\otimes1_c)$, by [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. Step 4 identifies that inverse image for $b=\beta_{C,\alpha}$ with the specified pairing. Applying the bijection proves the claimed transpose characterization and its uniqueness.
